solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Schoolchild's punishment, devising a cryptic clue for 'crows'?

indicators.note: these words announce that the solution is to be read as a clue whose answer is the quoted word

parts.note: read as wordplay, the two words of the solution give C (the Roman numeral for a hundred) followed by ROWS (lines), which spells this word

explanation.surface: A pupil kept in after school is made to write out a crossword clue for 'crows' as a penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works backwards: C is a hundred and ROWS are lines, which together spell CROWS.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing out a sentence one hundred times was a traditional British school penalty for misbehaving pupils.

clue.text: Dreadful, dreadful fate. Stuck in Hull with no end in view

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are stuck inside the shortened port name
the final letter of the city name is dropped, so its end is out of view

parts.note: the Yorkshire port, used for its letters

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters of fate are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone laments an awful fate: being marooned in the city of Hull with no prospect of escape.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is a port city in Yorkshire; the first 'Dreadful' is the definition and the second the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something so unpleasant that it provokes loathing; they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Must have fought ignoring the Queensberry rules, you say

indicators.note: signals that the word must be heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: a boxer who ignores the Queensberry rules might have struck with the knee, that is kneed an opponent

explanation.surface: A boxer is accused of having brawled dirtily, disregarding the official rules of the sport.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queensberry rules are the standard code of boxing; using the knee breaks them. KNEED sounds just like the solution, since the K is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A must-have is a necessity, something required; the noun sense of the solution matches this.

clue.text: Determine to make lovers' knot with last of twine

indicators.note: tying the letters in a knot tangles them into a fresh order
the final letter of twine is taken

explanation.surface: A sailor resolves to tie a lovers' knot, finishing it off with the tail end of the string.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knot' scrambles LOVERS plus E (the last of twine) into the solution.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide firmly on a course of action; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Would bait for it be water biscuit?

definitions.text: Would bait for it be water biscuit?

parts.words: Would bait for it be water biscuit?
parts.note: a dog is fed a dog biscuit, so a small shark with a canine name, living in the sea, might be lured with a biscuit dropped in the water

explanation.surface: An angler wonders whether a water biscuit, the crisp cracker, would serve as bait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water biscuit' reads as a plain cracker, but here it means a biscuit for a creature of the water, as a dog biscuit is for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: This small shark shares its first part with the pet that eats dog biscuits, hence the joke.

clue.text: Girl showing resistance within limits on a regular basis

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the selected letters
every other letter is taken, at regular intervals

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A girl is shown to resist, but only within set boundaries and on a routine basis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a regular basis' takes I, I, S from limits; 'within' puts R among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A common girl's name, also borne by the Greek goddess of the rainbow.

clue.text: Then, mixing right and a left, delight

indicators.note: mixing shakes up the letters of the first word into a new order

explanation.surface: A boxer throws a right and then a left, mixing punches to the crowd's delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' looks like a boxer's combination, but it only scrambles the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate or charm someone completely; both verbs mean to fill with pleasure.

clue.text: Is he taking off as an artist?

definitions.meaning: taking off means mimicking, so this asks about a performer who imitates famous people
a painter of the school of Monet and Renoir

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man is succeeding, rising as a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both a mimic of celebrities and a member of the French painting movement led by Monet.

clue.text: Capturing armed band is vital for winning

indicators.note: the first word captures the second, holding it within

parts.note: pressing means urgent, vital
a posse is a group of armed men gathered by a sheriff

explanation.surface: Taking an armed gang prisoner is essential if one is to win the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Winning in the sense of charming or attractive, making a good first impression.

clue.text: Say 'Put in writing,' evoking grumbles

indicators.note: the spoken word is put inside the abbreviation

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Someone told to put a complaint in writing grumbles about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like a link to the quotation but is the verb to be inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe complaining under one's breath, mumbling discontentedly.

clue.text: Are bright, coming from good family

parts.note: a litter is a family of young animals born together

explanation.surface: People from a good family are said to be bright.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that sparkle or shine are bright; the plural verb matches 'Are bright'.

clue.text: Taking out large gun, raging

indicators.note: taking out means removing a letter from the weapon

parts.note: a rifle is a gun

explanation.surface: Someone in a fury pulls out a big gun.
explanation.definitionFit: When a disease is rampant or widespread it is said to be raging, which the solution also describes.

clue.text: One in drawing's no oil painting

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the drawing

parts.note: a plan is a drawing; the 's is 'is'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An art critic notes that one of the works in a drawing show is not an oil painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no oil painting' is the British idiom for someone unattractive, not a comment on art.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying someone is no oil painting means they are unattractive, ordinary in looks.

clue.text: Cover up blame in statement

indicators.note: a statement is spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to take the rap is to take the blame

explanation.surface: Someone covers up the blame in their official statement.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap something is to cover it up, enclosing it in paper or cloth.

clue.text: Run in murderer with dog

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the name

parts.note: Cain, in Genesis, murdered his brother Abel
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Police run in a murderer along with his dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Scottish terrier breed, so it is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Drink, strong, not finished off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged
the word is unfinished, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A drink is strong and has not been finished off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' cuts STRONG to STRON, and 'off' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A snort is a quick nip of spirits, a small drink.

clue.text: Leaves out G in 'edge'

indicators.note: out suggests letters thrown out of order

explanation.surface: An instruction for spelling: leave the G out of the word edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves out G' looks like an instruction to delete, but 'out' scrambles LEAVES and G together.
explanation.definitionFit: The woven border of a fabric that stops it fraying is its finished edge.

clue.text: Feels hot and girl gets out of Levi's

indicators.note: the girl's name is removed from the jeans brand

parts.note: Vi is a girl's name, short for Violet

explanation.surface: A hot girl wriggles out of her Levi's jeans and feels better.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking VI from LEVIS leaves LES.
explanation.definitionFit: Handling something means touching and feeling it with the hands.

clue.text: Little blighter's bearing gift and grants

indicators.note: bearing means carrying inside

parts.note: an imp is a little blighter, a mischievous child; with the possessive it gives an S
an art is a skill or gift

explanation.surface: A mischievous child carries a present and hands out grants.
explanation.definitionFit: To give or bestow something, such as knowledge; both verbs mean to hand over.

clue.text: Refer fluctuating heart pains — has to be eradicated

indicators.note: fluctuating means shifting about, so the letters are rearranged
the letters of the short word are wiped out of the mix

explanation.surface: A doctor refers a patient whose heart pains come and go and must be eliminated.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H, A, S from HEARTPAINS and 'fluctuating' rearranges what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain is to relate or have reference to something, close to refer.

clue.text: Let off lead, goes over to frighten

indicators.note: in a down entry, going over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: the star is the lead in a show

indicators.note: off means the letters of the word are disordered

explanation.surface: A dog let off its lead runs over and frightens someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns LET into TLE; 'goes over' sets STAR above it.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle is to give a sudden fright or shock.

clue.text: Mind about horse causing destruction

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second

parts.note: to mind is to care
a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Take care around a horse in case it causes damage.
explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale slaughter or devastation, such as on a battlefield, is massive destruction.

clue.text: Rests before night on the tiles?

definitions.text: Rests before night on the tiles?

parts.words: Rests before night on the tiles?
parts.note: a night on the tiles is a night out on the town, a phrase from tomcats prowling roofs, so short sleeps before it suit a cat

explanation.surface: A partygoer has a few short sleeps before a big night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a night on the tiles' is British slang for a night of partying, from cats roaming the rooftops.
explanation.definitionFit: Short daytime sleeps are rests, and cats famously take them before prowling the roofs.

clue.text: By that time, a woman again is in occupation

indicators.note: the prefix occupies the inside of the woman

parts.note: a lady is a woman
RE- is a prefix meaning again

explanation.surface: By the time we arrived, a woman was once again living in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means before now or by then, the same as by that time.

clue.text: Roman's negative about the head of state

definitions.note: Roman's is read as 'Roman is', the definition being one particular Roman

indicators.note: the negative goes about the head of state

parts.note: no is a negative
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen, the British head of state

explanation.surface: A Roman says no to the head of state's proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Queen's cipher, Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman emperor who notoriously fiddled while Rome burned.

clue.text: In no way offensive

indicators.note: the street abbreviation goes in the denial

parts.note: nay is an old word for no
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A remark that is in no way offensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In no way' reads as one phrase, but each word has its own job.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpleasant or objectionable is offensive, a close synonym.

clue.text: Coat or only parts of one

definitions.text: Coat or only parts of one

parts.words: Coat or only parts of one
parts.note: a coat in heraldry is the shield of insignia borne by a family, while the sleeves of a jacket are just some parts of a coat

explanation.surface: A garment, or just some pieces of one.
explanation.definitionFit: Heraldic insignia form a coat of this name, and the sleeves of a coat are also called this.

clue.text: Portly figure's corseted and dull

indicators.note: a corset holds in, so the figure is held inside

parts.note: portly means fat
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a figure; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A stout person's figure is laced into a corset and looks dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat means lifeless or uninteresting, as a flat performance is dull.

clue.text: 'Capital' is 'big', see?

parts.note: OS is the abbreviation for outsize, big
lo means see, as in 'lo and behold'

explanation.surface: Someone argues that a capital city must be big.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital city.

clue.text: Try fencing the lot to produce vegetable

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a shot is an attempt or try
all is the lot

explanation.surface: A farmer tries to fence the whole plot so it will grow vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A small onion-like bulb used in cooking, so a vegetable.

clue.text: Salt mark's not come down on either side

definitions.text: not come down on either side

parts.note: a salt is a sailor, as is an AB, an able seaman
a stain is a mark; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A salt stain has not settled on either side of a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from voting for either side is to refuse to commit.

clue.text: What follows 'One's Labour…' is a different matter

definitions.meaning: in British politics, after a Labour government comes the other party, the Conservatives, whose members are called Tories
an idiom for something separate that will not be discussed now

explanation.surface: Someone starts a quotation about one's labours, then breaks off: that is another matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as ANOTHER S TORY: after Labour, another (government) is Tory. Tories are the British Conservative Party, Labour its rival.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock idiom for a separate issue, a different matter entirely.
